good_tf:
resource "azurerm_network_security_rule" "rdp" {
  name                        = "allow-rdp"
  priority                    = 100
  direction                   = "Inbound"
  access                      = "Allow"
  protocol                    = "Tcp"
  source_port_range           = "*"
  destination_port_range      = "3389"
  source_address_prefix       = "10.0.0.0/16" # FIX: restrict source to internal virtual network CIDR
  destination_address_prefix  = "*"
  resource_group_name         = "example-rg"
  network_security_group_name = "example-nsg"
}
why_it_matters: Setting source_address_prefix to '*' exposes TCP port 3389 directly to the public internet, allowing any remote IP address to initiate RDP handshakes against attached virtual machines.
Attackers scan public ranges for open port 3389 to launch brute-force password guessing or exploit unpatched vulnerabilities in the Remote Desktop Protocol service.
Restricting source_address_prefix to a trusted internal CIDR like 10.0.0.0/16 blocks unauthorized external traffic at the network security group before it touches the OS.
post_en:
You apply source_address_prefix = "*" on an inbound rule allowing destination port 3389.

Step 1: An internet scanner detects an open TCP socket on port 3389 at your public IP address.
Step 2: The attacker initiates Remote Desktop Protocol handshakes to enumerate local accounts and brute-force credentials.
Step 3: After authenticating into an interactive session, the attacker executes scripts to dump memory and pivot deeper into your virtual network.

Inbound network security rules that permit traffic to port 3389 from any source address are blocked.
Change source_address_prefix to a trusted private CIDR like 10.0.0.0/16.
